Subjective:
- Presenting complaint and trigger/exposure:
  • Reduced appetite, low energy and episodic shortness of breath/“palpitations,” especially when riding in a lift (no specific food, drug or environmental trigger identified).
- Symptom timeline and progression:
  • Loss of appetite ≈ 3–3.5 months.  
  • Weight loss ≈ 1 stone over ≈ 6 months.  
  • Short-of-breath/palpitations episodes occur “every time” in lifts; no limitation reported when walking a mile (although patient currently walks very little).
- ENT symptoms: none reported. Specifically denies or did not report throat swelling/closure sensation, voice change, dysphagia/odynophagia, drooling, nasal/ocular symptoms, stridor/noisy breathing, dyspnea at rest, facial/lip/tongue swelling, ear pain/hearing change, neck pain/swelling.
- Relevant past episodes and treatments: none.
- Allergies: not stated.
- Current medications:
  • Levothyroxine – patient stopped “since I changed doctor,” dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Relevant past medical history:
  • Under-active thyroid (hypothyroidism).
- Social context: Lives with wife (implied); no other support details provided.

Objective:
- Observable swelling: none reported.
- Airway/breathing: no stridor; patient subjectively short of breath only in lifts.
- Mental status: alert, interactive; mood described as low.
- Vitals and examination findings: Not recorded.
- Presence of another person during call: none.

Assessment:
- Fatigue, weight loss and episodic palpitations/SOB in a patient with untreated hypothyroidism.  
- No current ENT airway compromise.  
- Differential includes metabolic disturbance (thyroid dysfunction, anemia, vitamin deficiency) vs. anxiety/panic episodes (lift-related), cardiac arrhythmia.  
- No red-flag ENT findings at present.

Plan:
- Ordered general blood tests: thyroid function, full blood count, renal, liver profile, vitamins, etc. (doctor to send form; patient to phone support to schedule phlebotomy).
- Safety-net advice:  
  • Attend A&E immediately for chest pain, persistent vomiting, bowel habit change, or worsening shortness of breath.  
  • If feeling unwell before results return, contact service directly.
- Follow-up: Patient will receive text when results are back to book review; encouraged to call support line (03 00 …) to arrange blood draw. Physical examination to be arranged if blood tests unremarkable yet symptoms persist.
- Medication: Restarting levothyroxine not yet advised—pending blood results.

Quality checks
Missing/expected elements:
• Full allergy list.  
• Comprehensive medication list (other regular or OTC drugs).  
• ENT examination (airway, oral cavity, neck).  
• Vital signs.  
• Clarification on availability of auto-injector (not indicated but routinely checked in ENT allergy clinics).

Internal conflicts: none noted.

Transcript quality: Clear; minimal background noise.
